title: Proxy and Chain of Responsibility
idea: Proxy is a stand-in with the same interface that controls access to the real object. Chain of Responsibility passes a request along handlers until one deals with it.
points: A proxy implements the real object's interface, so callers cannot tell them apart.
Unlike a decorator, it controls access and often creates the real object itself.
In a chain, each handler either answers the request or forwards it to `next`.
The sender knows only the first handler; the chain's order sets the outcome.

hero.title: A refund request walks the chain

edges.label: start
edges.caption: The caller hands the request to the first handler only.

edges.label: too big
edges.caption: 150.0 is over the automatic limit, so `AutoRefund` forwards it.

edges.label: handled
edges.caption: `AgentRefund` can approve up to 200, so it answers and the chain stops.

edges.label: too big
edges.caption: A larger amount would travel on to `ManagerReview`, the catch-all.

edges.label: handled
edges.caption: The last handler always answers, so no request falls off the end.

code.title: Proxy
code.caption: A protection proxy that also opens the costly real object only when needed.

walk.text: The interface both the real object and the proxy implement.
`ArchiveReports` is costly to build; its constructor prints so you see when.
The proxy keeps the caller's role and a `real` field that starts empty.
It refuses the wrong role, builds the real object once, then delegates.
`main` uses two proxies; only the analyst's ever opens the archive.

code.title: Chain of Responsibility
code.caption: Three handlers, each with its own limit. The chain is built once in `main`.

walk.text: The base class stores `next` and forwards by default.
`AutoRefund` answers small amounts, otherwise calls `super.handle` to forward.
`AgentRefund` follows the same shape with a higher limit.
`ManagerReview` ends the chain and always answers.
`main` links the handlers and sends three amounts to the first one.

pitfalls: End every chain with a catch-all, or check the null `next` case explicitly.
Do not build a lazy proxy's real object in the constructor; that defeats it.
Keep a proxy's interface identical to the real one, or callers must know about it.

quiz.why: `AutoRefund` tests `amount <= 20`. Exactly 20.0 passes that test, so the first handler answers and nothing is forwarded.

takeaway: A proxy guards one object; a chain lets many handlers take turns.
